Author: Manoj Kumar Tiwari
Bench: Manoj Kumar Tiwari
 Office Notes,

Sl. or proceedings
 Date Court'S Or Judges'S Order

S No or directions and  Registrar's order  with Signatures  CRLA No. 193 of 2025  Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Hon'ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
1.
Mr. Arvind Vashisth, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Mr. Rajat Mittal, learned counsel for the appellant.
2. Mr. J.S. Virk, learned Additional Advocate General for the State of Uttarakhand.

3. This appeal is filed under Section 374(2) of Cr.P.C. against the judgment and order dated 07.03.2025 rendered by learned Sessions /Fast Track Special Court (POCSO), Dehradun in Special Sessions Trial No. 26 of 2022, whereby appellant has been convicted under Sections 376 and 120-B of I.P.C. and Sections 16/17 of POCSO Act.

He has been directed to undergo imprisonment for twenty years under Sections 376/120-B I.P.C. with fine of 50,000/- and, in default of payment of fine, he was sentenced to undergo further six months additional simple imprisonment.

4. Heard learned counsel for the parties on the bail application (IA No. 1 of 2025) moved on behalf of appellant and perused the record.
5. Appellant runs a Guest House at Selakui, District Dehradun, where the alleged incident took place.

It is contended by the learned counsel for the appellant that there is absolutely no evidence against the appellant to connect him with the crime; the cab driver, who dropped the victim at a place from where the co-accused brought the victim to appellant's guest house on a motorcycle, also did not state anything against the appellant; none of the employees of the guest house was examined before the Trial Court.
It is also contended that the victim neither in her 164 CrPC statement nor in her deposition before the Trial Court has stated anything against the appellant.

Thus, it is contended that there is absolutely no material on record connecting the appellant with the alleged offence and the appellant has been convicted only because he runs the guest house in question.
It is further contended by learned counsel for the appellant that appellant neither participated in, nor facilitated or had any knowledge of alleged incident.

1 6.

Learned State Counsel, per contra, submits that alleged incident took place at appellant's guest house and in the guest house register, the only name of co-accused has been indicated on 16.12.2021 and 19.12.2021, however, name of victim was not mentioned.

7. Having heard the rival submissions and considering the facts and circumstances of the case and without expressing any opinion on the final merits of the appeal, this Court thinks that a case for bail is made out.
8. Accordingly, Bail Application (IA No. 1 of 2025) is allowed.

Let the appellant - Sanjeev Aggarwal be released on bail during the pendency of this appeal on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned.
During pendency of the appeal the sentence imposed by trial court shall remain suspended.
(Subhash Upadhyay, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
